description: Internal personas — bank staff, specialist functions, and operational roles — who work within or across the bank's capabilities. Covers all roles with material interaction with regulated systems, customer data, or risk and compliance obligations, including SM&CR-designated Senior Managers.

personas.name: Relationship Manager
personas.description: A client-facing banker responsible for managing the end-to-end relationship with a portfolio of commercial, corporate, or HNW banking clients. Acts as the primary point of contact, coordinates credit applications, product introductions, and deal structuring. RM departure is the single largest attrition risk for commercial and wealth clients (30–40% of book at risk per industry data). Must complete SM&CR Certified Function requirements annually and maintain accurate CRM records.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier commercial bank may employ 200–800 Relationship Managers across SME, mid-market, corporate, and wealth segments

personas.name: Credit Analyst
personas.description: A specialist who assesses the creditworthiness of commercial, corporate, and retail lending applications. Constructs financial models, stress-tests cash flows, reviews management accounts, and prepares credit papers for approval committees. Works within PRA Basel 3.1 IRB model constraints and must apply PRA-approved PD/LGD/EAD models. Also supports annual credit reviews and covenant monitoring for existing facilities. Interacts heavily with the Risk Management and Commercial Banking capabilities.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier commercial bank may employ 50–200 Credit Analysts across retail, SME, and corporate credit teams

personas.name: Compliance Officer (MLRO)
personas.description: The Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) is the SM&CR-designated Senior Manager (SMF17) with personal accountability for the bank's AML and counter-terrorist financing programme. Receives internal SAR disclosures from staff, decides on NCA disclosure within 5 business days, and maintains the annual MLRO report to the Board. Also oversees sanctions screening, KYC governance, and coordinates with HMRC/FCA on supervisory compliance. Has regulatory reporting obligations that cannot be delegated below SMF level.
personas.volume_estimate: One designated MLRO (SMF17) per regulated entity; supported by a Financial Crime team of 20–100 analysts and compliance officers in a mid-tier bank

personas.name: Treasury Dealer
personas.description: A front-office trader responsible for managing the bank's FX, interest rate, and liquidity positions in the financial markets. Executes FX spot and forward trades, manages CHAPS settlement positions throughout the day, and hedges the bank's IRRBB and market risk exposures. Works within market risk limits set by the Risk Management capability under FRTB/VaR constraints. Must be an FCA-certified individual under SM&CR for dealing in investments as principal.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier commercial bank's treasury desk may have 5–30 dealers and traders across FX, rates, and liquidity positions

personas.name: Fraud Analyst
personas.description: An operations specialist who reviews transaction monitoring alerts generated by the bank's fraud detection systems (Featurespace ARIC, NetGuardians, NICE Actimize) and investigates suspected fraudulent transactions, APP fraud claims, and card disputes. First responder to APP fraud reimbursement claims — must triage, investigate, and approve or decline within the PSR 5-day window. Coordinates with the MLRO on cases that also have an AML dimension. Volume of alerts is a key operational cost driver — AI/ML false positive rates directly impact team efficiency.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank's fraud operations team may have 30–150 analysts managing thousands of daily transaction monitoring alerts

personas.name: Mortgage Underwriter
personas.description: A specialist responsible for assessing and approving residential mortgage applications against the bank's credit policy, PRA affordability rules, and MCOB suitability requirements. Reviews income evidence, credit bureau data, property valuations, and applicant vulnerability flags. Works within automated decisioning guardrails (scorecard + policy rules) and has manual override authority up to a defined delegation limit. Subject to SM&CR Certified Function obligations and FCA MCOB training requirements.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank may employ 30–150 mortgage underwriters across centralised and regional teams

personas.name: Branch Staff
personas.description: Front-line bank employees based in the branch network, including cashiers, customer service advisers, and branch managers. Handles cash transactions, identity-verified account opening, complaint resolution, mortgage appointments, and referrals to specialist teams. Branch numbers have declined sharply (from ~9,000 to under 4,000 UK branches 2015–2024) as digital substitution accelerates. Remaining branches increasingly focus on complex needs, vulnerable customers, and business banking relationships.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank with a selective branch network may employ 2,000–8,000 branch-based staff across 100–400 locations

personas.name: Wealth Advisor
personas.description: A qualified financial adviser or discretionary portfolio manager serving HNW and mass-affluent clients within the bank's wealth management division. Conducts suitability assessments, recommends investment strategies, monitors portfolios, and delivers periodic client reviews. Must hold appropriate FCA-approved qualifications (Chartered Financial Planner, IMC, or equivalent) and be registered on the FCA Financial Services Register as a certified individual under SM&CR. Subject to MiFID suitability rules and Consumer Duty fair value obligations.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank's wealth division may employ 100–500 qualified Wealth Advisors and portfolio managers

personas.name: Operations Staff
personas.description: Back-office processing staff covering payment operations (BACS file submission, CHAPS investigations, SWIFT message repair), trade finance document checking, and account maintenance. Handles manual exception queues generated by automated payment and compliance systems. Role is being progressively reduced by automation (STP rates above 99% for Faster Payments) but remains critical for high-value CHAPS investigations, SWIFT message repair, and trade finance document validation under ETDA.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank may employ 100–500 payments and operations processing staff, reducing as automation matures

personas.name: Senior Manager (SMF)
personas.description: An individual holding a PRA/FCA-approved Senior Manager Function (SMF) designation, with personal regulatory accountability for a defined area of the bank's activities and a documented Statement of Responsibilities. Includes roles such as CEO (SMF1), CFO (SMF2), CRO (SMF4), CTO (SMF24), MLRO (SMF17), Head of Compliance (SMF16), and prescribed responsibility holders. Any breach of a conduct rule exposes the SMF holder to FCA/PRA enforcement, financial penalties, or prohibition from the industry.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank will have 15–30 designated SMF holders at ExCo and board level

personas.name: IT Operations
personas.description: Technology staff responsible for the availability, performance, and security of the bank's core systems — including payment processing infrastructure, mobile and online banking platforms, and risk and compliance systems. Responsible for meeting the impact tolerance commitments for Important Business Services under PRA SS1/21 and FCA PS21/3. Must manage third-party cloud and SaaS providers as part of the bank's material outsourcing framework (SS2/21). On-call during payment system or digital banking outages.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank may have 200–800 IT operations, infrastructure, and DevOps staff across banking and payment systems

personas.name: Risk Model Validator
personas.description: An independent specialist who validates the bank's quantitative models (credit risk PD/LGD/EAD, FRTB market risk, IFRS 9 provisioning, fraud ML models) against PRA SS1/23 model risk management requirements. Must be organisationally independent from the model development teams. Produces validation reports that are reviewed by the Head of Model Risk and reported to the Board Risk Committee. AI/ML models require additional explainability and bias testing under DP5/22 and emerging AI Act obligations.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank may have 10–40 model validators in the Model Risk function, depending on model inventory size

personas.name: Customer Service Agent
personas.description: A telephone or digital-chat customer service agent handling inbound retail and SME customer queries — covering account queries, payment disputes, product enquiries, complaint acknowledgements, and vulnerability referrals. Must follow Consumer Duty consumer support outcome requirements — not designed to deter complaints or deflect customers from their rights. Handles Breathing Space notifications, APP fraud claim initiation, and FSCS temporary high balance queries. Interaction volume is being reduced by digital self-service but remains critical for complex and vulnerable customer journeys.
personas.volume_estimate: A mid-tier bank may employ 500–3,000 customer service agents across telephony, digital chat, and email support teams
